curriculum: The Dutch-taught Utrecht Computer Science bachelor totals 180 EC. The 135 EC major contains ten 7.5 EC compulsory courses, six 7.5 EC restricted electives and the 15 EC team Software Project. The generic example uses Imperative Programming and the first six listed electives. Algorithms and Data Analysis and Retrieval each contribute 7.5 EC of advanced electives and together meet the 15 EC advanced elective requirement. The separate 45 EC profiling space requires at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3 and courses must avoid overlap. The individual 15 EC thesis is a profiling option and does not replace the required team project. The two compulsory tutorials carry zero credits.
progression: Using the 2026 published teaching cycle as an illustration: Year 1 pairs Imperative Programming and Networks in period 1, Logic and the introductory project in period 2, Databases and Web Technology in period 3, and Data Structures and Graphics in period 4. Year 2 pairs Functional Programming and Software Engineering in period 1, Concurrency and Computational Intelligence in period 2, Algorithms and profiling in period 3, and IT Law and Data Analysis and Retrieval in period 4. In Year 3, Research Methods can precede the required two-period team Software Project, with the remaining profiling spread across the year. The identified pairs occupy distinct published timeslots. Future timetables may vary and profiling choices must fit available slots. The university invites eligible students to register directly. The public pages do not specify a current numeric project invitation threshold. No such number is assumed.
